key_insight: The thesis shows that in large action spaces, policy learning becomes tractable when actions are tied together through structured priors or latent representations, rather than treating every action independently.
engineering_relevance: This matters for recommendation, ranking, and decision systems with many actions because it offers scalable ways to learn from sparse feedback while controlling regret, bias, and variance.
method: meTS: a mixed-effect Thompson sampling method that shares statistical strength across actions.
dTS: a diffusion-inspired structured prior that captures similarity among actions for better exploration.
Off-policy learning: latent-variable structured direct methods plus concave policy-weighted objectives and pessimistic smoothing to stabilize importance-sampling estimates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports regret guarantees for the on-policy methods and optimization-vs-estimation analyses, plus PAC-Bayesian control of the bias-variance trade-off for the off-policy estimators.
watch_item: These methods rely on structured assumptions and careful optimization, so performance may degrade if the action dependencies or logging-policy coverage are misspecified.
paper_title: On-Policy and Off-Policy Learning for Large Action Spaces
